market_context: United States/general English; home storage of cooked fish and seafood leftovers
title: How long does cooked fish last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long does cooked fish last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Cooked fish and seafood can be refrigerated for 3–4 days at 40 °F/4 °C or below. Chill it promptly and freeze portions you will not use.
seo.search_intent: Learn how long cooked fish keeps refrigerated and how to cool, store and reheat it safely.

excerpt: USDA recommends using cooked fish and other seafood within 3–4 days when refrigerated at 40 °F (4 °C) or below. Refrigeration slows bacterial growth but does not stop it, so prompt chilling matters as much as the calendar.
content_html:
Cooked fish should not stay in the refrigerator until it finally smells suspicious. USDA's practical storage window is 3–4 days at 40 °F (4 °C) or below.

Think 3–4 days, not a week

Cooked fish and other seafood can be safely refrigerated for 3 to 4 days. A fillet cooked on Monday should therefore generally be eaten by Thursday or Friday, assuming it was chilled promptly and kept cold.

The refrigerator slows microbial growth; it does not freeze time.

Chill leftovers promptly

Perishable food should not sit at room temperature for hours before refrigeration. The general USDA rule is to refrigerate leftovers within about 2 hours, or sooner in very hot conditions.

Large quantities cool faster when divided into shallow containers rather than packed into one deep, warm container.

Smell does not extend the deadline

An ammonia-like or sour odor, slime or mold are obvious reasons to discard fish. The reverse is not reliable: food can look and smell normal even after being stored too long.

So a normal smell on day six is not evidence that the 3–4 day guidance no longer applies.

Freezing buys more time

USDA lists about 3 months as a good-quality target for cooked fish at 0 °F (−18 °C) or below. Frozen food can remain safe longer when continuously frozen, but texture and flavor gradually decline.

If you know you will not eat a portion within the next few days, freezing it early usually gives a better result than waiting until day four.

What about reheating?

USDA uses 165 °F (74 °C) as the reheating target for leftovers. Fish that will be served cold does not need reheating if it was originally cooked and stored safely.

Mixed dishes follow the same clock

Putting two-day-old fish into a casserole, rice bowl or sauce does not reset its age. The storage history of the ingredients still matters, so date leftovers from the earliest relevant cooking step.

Bottom line

Use cooked fish within 3–4 refrigerated days. Cool it quickly, keep the refrigerator at 40 °F/4 °C or below and freeze portions you will not use in that window.

faq.question: Can I eat cooked fish after five days?
faq.answer: USDA's conservative refrigerator guidance is 3–4 days. Beyond that, discarding it is the safer choice.

faq.question: How long does cooked fish keep in the freezer?
faq.answer: For best quality, USDA lists about 3 months at 0 °F/−18 °C or below.

faq.question: Do I have to reheat leftover fish?
faq.answer: Not if it will be eaten cold and was stored safely. If reheating leftovers, 165 °F/74 °C is the standard USDA target.
